reasons: Cited Section 17(b) (p0118) gives the Customer an unconditional right to terminate 'at any time' on 90 days' written notice with no early-termination fee, which satisfies the fallback (60–90 days' notice, no penalty) on its material terms; per playbook classification semantics a clause at the fallback is compliant and should not be redlined.

No Vendor termination-for-convenience right appears in the cited termination provisions — Section 17 limits termination to Customer notice (17(b)) or either party for default/insolvency (p0128) — so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience right on <90 days) is not present.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artefact: 17(b) grants termination 'at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice' without using the words 'for convenience'/'without cause'. Substance controls.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed (redline text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was generated, which is the expected output.
The rationale correctly notes the sub-elements short of preferred (30 days' notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees) as observations rather than escalating them to a deviation.
